what_happened: The operator queued a speed request, "cut B", with a hard numeric target: the full test suite in under 6 minutes, later 7. Nobody had measured whether that was reachable. Three attempts (eebk, xgk9, y179) cost about $9 and 4 hours. Each cut Athena's test check from about 12 minutes to 7.4–7.8 minutes. Each was rejected for missing the number, so none landed, even though the improvement was real. The rabbit-hole guard did not flag the line of work after the second rejection for the same unmet target.
cause: A speed request sets its target from assumption rather than from measured stage durations and a measured floor. Neither request intake nor the reading checks a numeric performance target against a baseline or a feasibility measurement. Acceptance is a pass/fail threshold, so real partial gains count as failures. Nothing stops repeated retries of a line of work that was rejected for the same unmet number.
prevention: Add a check at intake and in the reading for any request with a numeric performance target. It would require a recorded measured baseline and either a measured feasibility figure or a "measured improvement over baseline" criterion. It would refuse or warn on a bare threshold. Make the rabbit-hole guard count rejections per unmet target and hold the third attempt until the operator re-measures or resets the target.
proposed_request:
Speed up Athena's test check (cut B). First, measure the current full-suite duration (baseline, about 12 minutes) and the per-test time breakdown on this repository, and record both in the job's output. Then make changes that reduce the full-suite time. Acceptance:
- The job reports the measured baseline and the measured after-change duration, using the same method for both.
- The after-change duration is at least 30% lower than the baseline, which the earlier attempts' 7.4–7.8 minutes would satisfy.
- No test is removed or weakened, and the full suite still passes.
Do not set an absolute target of 6 or 7 minutes. If further gains look possible, list them with estimated savings as a follow-up and do not implement them in this job.
